investigator.method: Full escalation ladder against the LIVE public site (not a synthetic fixture): PASSIVE_STATIC via curl against https://www.hardclubporto.com/ and its agenda page, STRUCTURAL via curl against a first-party AJAX endpoint publicly referenced in the page's own funcoes.js, then BROWSER_OBSERVATION via a Playwright MCP browser session loading the public agenda page as an ordinary visitor. The Level 3 finding (that the AJAX endpoint's date field includes month text only once a prior page load has established a session cookie) was then independently reproduced without any browser via a two-step curl flow, and a small dependency-free, no-network offline script (evidence/offline-proof.mjs) deterministically parsed the retained fixtures to confirm the sampled fields.

probe_history.reason:
A plain unauthenticated GET of the official agenda page (evidence/agenda.html, and the home page evidence/home.html) returns an empty client-rendered shell for the main event list:
    with zero server-rendered event cards. No JSON-LD/schema.org, no RSS/ICS/alternate link, no embedded JSON was found anywhere in either response. The only date-bearing content present in the raw initial HTML is a small footer/nav-menu widget listing the 3 nearest events with day+abbreviated-month text (e.g. "12 Set") -- not the full listing, and not itself the site's main agenda content.

Inspected the page's own public JS (evidence/funcoes.js) and found it publicly references a first-party AJAX endpoint used to populate the event list client-side: GET /include/ajax_functions.php with action=load-agenda (list) and action=loadevent (per-event price/description), both invoked directly by the page's own script, not brute-forced. A structural GET of the load-agenda action with no prior page load in the same cookie jar (evidence/ajax-agenda.html, and independently evidence/ajax-noprior.html using browser-like headers) returns the full 22-event HTML fragment, but its "data" field carries ONLY a bare day-of-month (e.g. "11 "), never a month -- reproducing exactly the ambiguity the prior sources/porto.json investigation (BOTM-RESEARCH-PORTO-SOURCES-01 / PORTO-COVERAGE-02) recorded for this same candidate. The loadevent action was also structurally probed (first with an incorrect id parameter guessed from a numeric data-rel attribute, evidence/ajax-loadevent-badparams-attempt.html, which returned an empty detail template; then correctly, using the anchor's own id/URL-slug attribute exactly as the page's own click handler does, evidence/ajax-loadevent-johnny-hooker.html) -- it exposes price and a free-text description, but no month/year field either. The archive page (evidence/arquivo.html) was also checked for a month/year filter widget; none exists.

A controlled Playwright browser session loaded https://www.hardclubporto.com/PT/agenda/ as an ordinary, unauthenticated visitor (no login, no CAPTCHA interaction). Its captured network traffic (evidence/browser-network-capture.txt) showed the SAME endpoint/action/parameters as the Level 2 probe returning a DIFFERENT response: full "DD Mon" day+month text for every event (e.g. "12 Set", "01 Out", "29 Jan"), confirmed independently in the rendered DOM (evidence/browser-accessibility-snapshot.txt). The only variable that changed versus the Level 2 probe was that the browser had already performed a normal prior GET of /PT/agenda/ in the same session/cookie jar before the AJAX call. This was then independently reproduced with NO browser at all via a plain two-step curl flow -- GET /PT/agenda/ once to establish a PHPSESSID cookie, then GET the AJAX endpoint with that same cookie and a Referer header (evidence/ajax-agenda-session.html + evidence/headers-ajax-agenda-session.txt, byte-for-byte matching the browser-observed shape for all 22 events). This resolved the Level 1/2 gap and revealed that a genuine, non-browser, two-step HTTP acquisition path exists. No access control, CAPTCHA, or challenge was encountered, so this is logged SUFFICIENT (not BLOCKED); escalation terminates here -- Level 4 (browser as the permanent collector) is not needed since the resolved path requires no persistent browser rendering.

start_date.notes: Day-of-month + abbreviated Portuguese month (e.g. "12 Set", "01 Out", "29 Jan") IS reliably present for every sampled event, but only once the two-step session-gated HTTP flow documented in probe_history level 3 is used (evidence/ajax-agenda-session.html; deterministically confirmed offline in evidence/offline-proof-output.txt, which shows 0 of 22 events carrying a 4-digit year in this field and all 22 matching a "DD Mon" shape). The CALENDAR YEAR is never stated directly by the source in any structural response observed (list fragment, detail fragment, or event detail page) -- this matches, and this investigation's own new evidence confirms, the gap the prior sources/porto.json entry (hard-club-porto) recorded. The URL slug carries a trailing year-like suffix (e.g. "-2026", "-2027") that appears consistent with chronological ordering, but the source does not document this as a canonical date field, and this investigation deliberately does not infer a year from list sequence/order per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's explicit prohibition. Sporadic first-party free-text corroboration exists for SOME events (the U.D.O. entry's own description literally contains the numeral "2027", matching its slug suffix -- evidence/ajax-loadevent-udo.html) but this is not a structured, universally-present field and cannot be relied on for every event. Net effect versus the prior investigation: day+month is now a materially stronger, genuinely resolved finding (not previously known to be obtainable); year remains honestly unresolved and requires a deliberate policy decision, not a fabricated value.

time.notes: The "local_hora" field gives a room label plus a 24-hour local time (e.g. "Sala 2 : 20H00"), consistently present for every sampled event, but with no explicit timezone/UTC marker anywhere in the response -- a floating local time only, per docs/OBSERVATION_PIPELINE.md's certainty model, not promoted to a confirmed UTC instant.

end.notes: No end time or end date is exposed anywhere in the retained list fragment, detail fragment, or event detail page for any sampled event.

venue_location.value: Hard Club, Praça do Infante D. Henrique, Porto, Portugal (Mercado Ferreira Borges building)
venue_location.notes: Site-wide address from the footer (evidence/home.html, evidence/agenda.html) and explicit building-name confirmation from the about page (evidence/o-hard-club.html). Each individual event additionally carries its own room label ("Sala 1" or "Sala 2") in the same "local_hora" field used for time -- e.g. Johnny Hooker plays "Sala 2".

source_record_id.notes: The event's own URL-path slug (e.g. "johnny-hooker-euro-tour-2026-2026") is used consistently, by the source itself, as: (a) the list-fragment anchor's own "id" DOM attribute, (b) the canonical event-detail page URL segment (/PT/evento/{slug}/), and (c) the "id" parameter the page's own click handler (callEvento in evidence/funcoes.js) passes to the loadevent AJAX action to fetch that exact event's detail. This matches docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's stable-identifier rule: "derived from a deterministic source property whose own stability is itself evidenced (e.g. a permalink URL slug the source uses as its own canonical path)". IMPORTANT for any future collector: the fragment ALSO carries a numeric "data-rel" attribute (1, 2, 3, ...) that looks like an id but is only a page-load position index that resets across pagination "start" values -- confirmed NOT stable and must not be used as source_record_id (this was the source of one failed structural probe, evidence/ajax-loadevent-badparams-attempt.html, when the numeric value was tried first).

event_url.notes: Canonical per-event detail page URL, directly built from the site's own anchor href in the list fragment (evidence/ajax-agenda-session.html) and independently confirmed by fetching that exact URL (evidence/event-detail-johnny-hooker.html).

price.notes: Exposed only via a second, per-event AJAX call (action=loadevent, keyed by the event's own URL slug), not in the main list fragment. Confirmed for multiple sampled events at different price shapes: Johnny Hooker "25€- 55€", U.D.O. "45€" (flat), Moonspell Invicta Halloween "32,21€" (flat, comma decimal), +351 Festival Urbano "22€-30€" (range). The same response also carries an external ticketing link (e.g. q2ingressos.com.br for Johnny Hooker) and a free-text description, both venue-authored first-party content, not treated here as third-party authority.

blockers.description: No structural response ever exposes a calendar YEAR for any event -- only 'DD Mon' (day + abbreviated Portuguese month). A collector must not fabricate a year. The only source-provided corroboration observed is sporadic first-party free-text tour-description wording (e.g. the U.D.O. entry's description literally mentions '2027'), which is not present for every event and is not a structured field; the URL slug's trailing year-like suffix is suggestive but undocumented by the source as a stable date signal. A deliberate, explicit year-resolution policy (e.g. a documented today-relative rollover heuristic, consistent with this project's existing date-certainty conventions) needs to be decided by a human before activation -- this investigation does not invent one.

The full 'DD Mon' event-list fragment is only returned once the requesting HTTP client has first performed a normal GET of /PT/agenda/ (or another page in the same session) to establish a PHPSESSID cookie, and then repeats that same cookie plus a Referer header on the AJAX call. A cookie-naive single-request fetch silently returns day-only text with no error and no different HTTP status -- any future collector must implement this two-step flow explicitly, or it will silently regress to the ambiguous day-only data this investigation's own Level 1/2 probes hit.

The list fragment's own 'data-rel' attribute is a small sequential integer that resets across pagination and must never be used as source_record_id -- only the anchor's own 'id' attribute / URL slug should be used (see field_assessment.source_record_id.notes).

reasons: Levels 1 and 2 (passive/static, structural) reproduced exactly the ambiguity the prior sources/porto.json investigation (BOTM-RESEARCH-PORTO-SOURCES-01 / PORTO-COVERAGE-02) recorded for this candidate: day-of-month only, never a month, in a naive single-request fetch of the site's own AJAX endpoint.

Level 3 (browser observation) resolved that specific gap and produced a genuinely new finding, not a re-assertion of the old one: the SAME endpoint returns full day+month ('DD Mon') text for every event once a normal prior page load has established a session cookie -- independently reproduced with NO browser at all via a plain two-step curl flow (evidence/ajax-agenda-session.html).

Title, room+time, venue/address, per-event price, ticket link, and a reasonably provable stable source_record_id (the event's own canonical URL slug) are all reliably, deterministically extractable -- confirmed offline against retained fixtures with zero failures (evidence/offline-proof.mjs, evidence/offline-proof-output.txt).

The one genuinely unresolved gap is the calendar YEAR: the source never states it directly, in any structural response observed, for any event. Only sporadic free-text tour-description wording corroborates a year for some events, never as a structured field. Per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md this investigation must not infer a year from list sequence/order or invent one -- so field_assessment.start_date is honestly recorded PARTIAL, not PROVEN, and a deliberate year-resolution policy decision is needed from a human before this could honestly be marked READY_FOR_ACTIVATION.

Recorded as HUMAN_REVIEW rather than DEFER because the acquisition path itself is genuinely strong, non-browser, reproducible, and a materially better outcome than the prior investigation reached -- the remaining question is a deliberate policy call about year-handling, not a technical or access blocker; DEFER would understate how close this candidate now is.
